questions.question: Trace the path of a sperm cell from where it is produced to where it leaves the body, naming the glands that add fluid on the way.
questions.expected_answer: Testis (produced in the coiled tubules), epididymis (stored and matured), sperm duct (moved by muscular contractions), past the seminal vesicles and prostate gland (and Cowper's glands), which add fluid to form semen, into the urethra and out through the penis.

questions.question: Describe how an egg released at ovulation reaches the uterus, and state where fertilisation normally takes place.
questions.expected_answer: At ovulation a mature follicle bursts and releases the egg from the ovary. The fringed funnel of the oviduct catches it, and it is carried along the oviduct by beating cilia and muscular contractions over about three to four days, because it cannot move itself. Fertilisation normally takes place in the upper part of the oviduct.

questions.question: Give three structural differences between a sperm cell and an egg cell and relate one of them to its function.
questions.expected_answer: Any three, for example: sperm is small (about 0,05 mm) while the egg is large (about 0,1 mm); sperm has a tail and swims while the egg cannot move; sperm has a middle piece full of mitochondria while the egg has a large cytoplasm with a food store; sperm has an acrosome with enzymes while the egg has a jelly coat; sperm carries X or Y while the egg always carries X. Function example: mitochondria release energy for swimming, or the food store nourishes the early embryo, or the acrosome digests a path into the egg.
